sections.what: Lists the steps that build the backend image: base image, system tools, Python packages, code copy, data folder, port and start command.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the backend reproducible on any machine.
sections.watch_out: Copying everything can put secrets into the image. Remove the reload flag before production use.

summary: Recipe that packs the backend and its Python packages into a container that starts the API on port 8000.
purpose: Lets the backend run the same way on any machine.
why: Likely reason: a consistent environment. The reload flag suggests the image is meant for development.
how: Starts from a slim Python 3.11 image, sets the work folder to app, installs build tools and PostgreSQL headers, installs the packages in requirements.txt, copies all backend files, creates the research cache folder, exposes port 8000, and starts uvicorn with reload on.
inputs: requirements.txt, all backend files and the base Python image.
outputs: A container image that serves the API on port 8000.
risks: The copy-everything step also copies any .env file holding keys, unless a .dockerignore file excludes it; none is in the packet. The reload flag is for development and makes production behaviour unpredictable. Installing PostgreSQL headers suggests a PostgreSQL database, but the config defaults to SQLite.
debug: For build failures, read the failing step and check requirements.txt. If the API is unreachable, check the port mapping and that the app listens on all addresses.
